name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Balderson holds a roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Balderson's win odds near 95%
No public polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Balderson's incumbency, and his roughly $2.2 million-to-$140,000 fundraising edge over Jerrad Christian all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets price the race near 95% Republican. No polling or ratings suggest a competitive race, so the forecast stays close to fundamentals.
model.watch: Any public polling showing Christian within single digits or a major influx of outside Democratic spending would be the clearest sign this race deserves re-rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 12th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Troy Balderson is seeking another term after being renominated. The fundamentals strongly favor the GOP: the district's partisan lean sits near R+15, and Balderson enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised about $2.2 million to Jerrad Christian's $140,000, with more than $1 million in cash on hand.

Prediction markets give Balderson roughly a 95% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings indicate the race is competitive. Christian would need an unusually favorable national environment plus significant outside investment to close a gap of this size. The forecast expects Balderson to win by a wide margin, and the seat is rated Safe Republican. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room for surprise in either direction.
